column2: International Institute of Social History, Amsterdam
column4: *** ANSWERED 10 Sep 2026. *** Their Latin American periodicals are digitised and OCR'd at degruyterbrill.com/database/lalp/start. Their archivist searched Lerena and its variants: nothing. Re-run here the same day and the null holds - the 171 "Lerena" hits are the Conde de Lerena of the 1787 Spanish census and a Montevideo street called Osimani y Llerena; the 16 "Lerina" hits are OCR breakage of "ballerina". They will scan specific items at 0.50 euro each via repro@iisg.nl, but no target has been identified.

column2: Western Cape Archives and Records Service
column4: *** The most valuable unread document in the project. *** A South African death notice names the deceased's parents at question 19. It carries a stated prediction: it should say JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA. Gmail 1a087da08db5ca31.

TNA BT 27/0420 p.68 (Harlech Castle, 9 Sep 1903) and BT 27/0448 (Walmer Castle, 9 Apr 1904). The index carries no forename; the image very often does. findmypast's tile viewer will not render in this browser. Two minutes elsewhere.

column2: State Library of Queensland, South Bank
column4: FamilySearch says "Image Available - access the site at a FamilySearch centre or affiliate library". SLQ IS an affiliate. Open ark 1:1:ZYWT-S86Z on their wifi and photograph the WHOLE card: Ricardo is recorded as "Son", so there is a household with a head - almost certainly Pablo Armando, in the month Mary Septima died. Also try 1:1:ZYWT-S8N2 and the Cape estate ark 3:1:3Q9M-C913-K9H3-D.
